### problem_chain

Root problem (what the customer asks): "you want whatever you owe for those restored months put on the card the region already has on file for you" — the region's draft through the method on file, `prime_ext_draft_on_file_method` ("the amount the region draws through the payment method an enrollment keeps on file when the beneficiary asks for an amount owed ... to be collected that way"). `payment_method: recurring_card` is the method on file.

Prerequisite sentences of the root rule, each judged on the raw DB at 2026-10-14:

1. "A draft toward a back-billed installment is made only after every month from the month after the old paid-through date recorded on the enrollment's reinstatement review to the month before the current one lies inside the coverage period of an installment charge on the account."
   - Old paid-through date on the review: `appeal_cases.98c33fad….initial_determination_date = 2026-03-31` (the appeal charter takes it from the enrollment's disenrollment date). Span: April through September 2026.
   - Charges on the account cover Dec 2025-May 2026 and Oct 2026 (`33cc679b`, `77f1484d`, `19295b8e`, `913064af`, `c2d80912` Apr, `7c847e85` May, `fb771c45` Oct). June, July, August, September lie inside no charge → **unmet at the opening**.
   - Write that brings it about: the policy whose rule bills "months of its restored coverage that carry no installment charge" of an enrollment "that an Enrollment Reinstatement Review brought back" — `prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up` (`post_catch_up_installment_4baf2609`). The other charge-posting policy (first-installment supplement) is scoped to the months a first installment owes (effective 2020-01-01; its own figure on this account is 0.00), so it is not a candidate.
2. "No draft is made on an account until the region has refunded the duplicate payment found on it."
   - The duplicate the charter defines: "the installment ... carrying the largest single payment posted to the enrollment's fee account" — the 50.00 EFT payment `3d6ebbce…` (2026-07-16) against the April charge `c2d80912…`, which also carries 32.51 (`f117d739…`). Only a 2.00 refund (`8e81c5f0…`) stands against it; the duplicate policy still owes 40.49 (below) → **unmet at the opening**. Near-miss: February `19295b8e…` also carries two payments (32.51 card + 10.00 EFT); it is not the largest single payment.
   - Resolver: `prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund` (`refund_duplicate_payment_360f0d4a`).
3. "The region does not draw a back-billed installment until the installment of the current month stands paid in full."
   - Current month's installment: October `fb771c45…` 32.51; 20.00 paid (`8f97e9f9…`), 5.00 refunded against that payment (`b46fe3a9…`) → net 15.00 < 32.51 → **unmet at the opening** (also unmet on the gross 20.00).
   - Resolver: the beneficiary-authorised one-time bank draft toward an installment, `prime_ext_current_installment_payment` (`pay_current_installment_by_bank_draft_694809d0`, owner=user). The region's draft on file cannot be the resolver: it is the blocked root, and on the opening world it would draw 0.00 toward October (computed below), leaving it unpaid.

Derived tree: draft (root) <- catch_up (value_input: moves `dd_target` to the catch-up and its open amount); draft <- duplicate_refund (value_input: `dd_adjust`); draft <- current_installment_payment (value_input: `dd_adjust`). n = 3 prerequisite problems, 3 value_input edges (≥ max(n−1,1) = 2), no cycle, one owner=user write (current installment payment). Each child has no prerequisite of its own.

Topological order: {catch_up, duplicate_refund, current_installment_payment} in any order, then draft.

Load-bearing runs (`t0.py`, replay through the real tools, draft amount):

- skip catch-up: 0.00 (target becomes October, already overpaid)

Every edge bears weight.

Parallel-edge terminal state: the three children write different rows (a charge, a refund against `3d6ebbce`, a payment against `fb771c45`); none reads a quantity another writes in a way that changes its value (duplicate refund's window ends with September and its largest-payment pick is 50.00 either way; current payment reads only October's rows; catch-up reads no Oct-14 row). Any order gives the same terminal state.

Tools judge no prerequisite: every tool body in `task_tools.py` writes one ledger row and moves `fee_balance_due`; none checks status, coverage, refunds or order (`_difficulty.md` § action_binding_and_uuids).

The tree read from policy and world alone has three prerequisite problems under the draft; comparison with the declared `prerequisite` field (three edges: catch_up value_input state, duplicate_refund value_input action, current_installment_payment value_input state) — isomorphic.

**W1 — catch-up** (`post_catch_up_installment_4baf2609`, agent). Tier Retiree Group A, annual individual 390.12, family 780.24.
- Rate: not fee-exempt; arrangement individual; monthly charges of 32.51 = individual share → 1/12 × 390.12 = 32.51.
- First month: review decided overturned; documents: `statement_of_good_cause` (`f312a1ad…`), `medical_records` (`de4c0431…`), no `proof_of_payment` → "starts with the month after the old paid-through date the review recorded" → April 2026.
- Last month: filed 2026-06-10, decided 2026-07-08, 28 calendar days ≤ `decision_deadline` 30 (appeal.yaml, Enrollment Reinstatement Review) → "runs through the month before the current month" → September 2026.
- Span April-September = 6 months. Already charged: April (`c2d80912`), May (`7c847e85`) → 4 left (Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep). Billed by Select: Select charge `7105638c…` monthly, coverage begins 2026-07-01 → July left out → 3 months (Jun, Aug, Sep).
- Amount 3 × 32.51 = **97.53**. On the opening world (its own handling time) the compute gives 97.53.
- Coverage period: "from the first day of the first month it bills to the last day of the last month it bills". Primary reading: the months it still bills are Jun, Aug, Sep → **2026-06-01 to 2026-09-30**. Second reading: the catch-up's first month (April) → 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30. The rule uses "bills" both for the span ("A catch-up installment bills the month in which the reinstatement review was decided") and for the months left ("the number of months it still bills"), so the start date admits two readings; the end date (2026-09-30) and the amount are the same under both, and the draft is 22.51 under both (replayed). Flagged for the comparison.

- Value: individual fee 390.12; installment monthly → 32.51.

- Excess: 82.51 − 32.51 = 50.00. Earlier refunds against the latest payment: 2.00 → left 48.00.
- Shortfall since the duplicate (posted months April-September, "other than the refunded installment"): charges posted Apr-Sep other than April = May 32.51; payments posted in those months other than on April = 25.00 (`eca1ac89`, 2026-07-10); refunds other than of its latest payment = 0 → 7.51. - Held back: 7.51 (some shortfall, below 48.00). Refund = min(50.00, 48.00 − 7.51) = **40.49**, against **`3d6ebbce-35a2-474f-ac59-3db7b7810642`**, back through EFT (the tool copies the payment's method). Same value at any position in the sequence.

**W3 — current installment payment** (`pay_current_installment_by_bank_draft_694809d0`, owner=user; the agent hands the step to the beneficiary).

**W4 — draft on file (root)** (`run_draft_on_file_method_99529347`, agent), after W1-W3.

## findings

**0-F1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED: no computation of this task meets the factor bounds once the structurally void factors are struck; the task's only cross-difficulty factors are among them.**
- Symptom: GT declares 5 factors on each of 4 computations, each bearing weight on this world (figures above). Surviving the ladder tests: catch-up 0, duplicate refund 2, current payment 2, draft 4 with 1 `parameter` as labelled.
- Root cause: charter-global G1 (fee-exempt rung unreachable — struck in all four computations), G4 (catch-up first/last month turn on "decided overturned" and a good-cause statement, which every catch-up customer has), G5 (catch-up months-charged/Select, duplicate earlier-refunds/shortfall, payment received/owed-again ladders are one arithmetic step in three rungs). `_difficulty.md` § findings.
- Demonstration on this world: the struck factors bear weight numerically (table above), but each is struck for its ladder, not its weight: e.g. catch_up_first_month — this customer's review is decided overturned with `statement_of_good_cause` `f312a1ad…` on file, as every reinstated customer's must be (appeal charter: "A reinstatement is decided overturned only when a statement of good cause is on file for the case"), so the only live split is proof of payment (absent here); duplicate_earlier_refunds — the 2.00 refund taken off equals the "refunds already issued" rung, and with no refund that rung gives the fall-through's 0. Cross-difficulty requirement: the task's cross-difficulty factors (catch_up_first_month, catch_up_last_month on appeal; catch_up_months_billed_by_select on select) are all struck, so no surviving factor decides its tier from another difficulty's records.
- Affected: `prime.extended.yaml` factors of all four claimed policies; `tasks/0.json` `computations[*].factor_sensitivity`, `design_rationale` [Factor card] "Per-task floors".
- Relation to previous revisions: first audit.

**0-C1 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED (proof text): the load-bearing figure for skipping the duplicate refund is misstated.**
- Evidence: `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1].skipped_effect`: "the April duplicate stays as excess on the other installments (50.48 net of the May shortfall and with the February overpayment)". Recomputed (`t0.py`, writes W1+W3 without W2): payments on other installments 285.06 − every refund 7.00 − other charges 227.57 = **50.49** (April 48.00 + February 10.00 − May 7.51).
- Consequence: the asserted figure is wrong by 0.01; the conclusion it supports (draft 0.00, so the edge bears weight) holds under the recomputed 50.49.
- Affected: `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1]`.

**0-P1 — proof text (SOURCE-POLICY, single-resolver claims): two factual sentences in `design_rationale` are false although their conclusions hold by scope.**
- "Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: the catch-up posting (no other policy posts charges for past months)" — `prime_ext_first_installment_supplement` posts charges whose coverage includes past months (task 1's supplement covers September 2026). The single-resolver conclusion holds on the two policies' scope sentences (`_difficulty.md` § prerequisite_sentences).
- "Exactly one write brings it about in this difficulty: the beneficiary's one-time payment (the draft policy itself goes toward the back-billed installment, not the current one)" — on the opening world the draft rule goes toward October, the current installment ("otherwise it is toward the installment whose coverage period begins latest"); it is excluded as a resolver because it would draw 0.00 (excess 45.49 against an open 12.51) and because it is the blocked root, not for the stated reason.
